decisions.reason: The caption requirement already mandates white text with no text effects. Narrowing the separate visual-editing prohibition to heavy animations does not change that state.
B-roll integration is an independent rule introduced by another clause of the same message and already has a matching Event; the visual-animation change does not alter it.
The source decision concerns heavy animations and flashy transitions, not selection of the brand-specified caption font.
Background-music volume is independent of visual animation restrictions and is already represented by its own same-message Event.
Narrative completeness and standalone understandability are unaffected by the change to prohibited visual treatments; the same message's narrative clarification is already represented separately.
The visual-style change does not alter the assigned batch count or delivery obligation, whose same-message changes are already represented.
Prohibiting heavy animations and flashy transitions does not change the current substantive-moment selection standard.
The approval-before-publication workflow is independent of the visual-animation rule and is already established by its own clause and Event.
The visual-treatment modification does not change the permitted source collection or source-exclusion rule.
The source message does not modify hook selection or the requirement to follow the brand guidelines for hooks.
The visual-animation modification does not change the existing 70-to-85-second duration state.
A 12-clip launch batch with revised visual rules does not necessarily resume or modify the deferred monthly target of 140 approved clips.
